title: Runtime: select tiered batching defaults from batching_tier + workload signals
creator: Sofia Ivanova
description:
Problem
Customers (and internal services) need safe, predictable defaults for batching that align with intent: optimize for low tail latency vs balanced performance vs cost-efficiency. Today, most batching knobs are tuned manually and vary by route/model; incorrect settings frequently cause p95 spikes (queueing) or cost blowups (under-batching).

This ticket implements runtime logic to:
1) Interpret a high-level `batching_tier` (fast | standard | cost_efficient).
2) Combine tier intent with workload signals (streaming vs non-streaming, prompt length bucket, observed concurrency/arrival rate, model family, GPU SKU) to compute a set of scheduler/batching parameters.
3) Enforce precedence rules so explicit per-route overrides always win and existing configs remain backwards compatible.

Scope
- Runtime tier selection entrypoint (config -> effective scheduler params).
- Workload-signal extraction (minimal v1 signals; no new scheduling research).
- Deterministic mapping to a parameter set (with guardrails / clamps).
- Hooks for model-family / GPU-specific overrides (pulled from model registry where available; default tables otherwise).
- Logging/trace annotations to make “why did we pick these values?” debuggable (full explain endpoint is handled elsewhere, but runtime must emit the fields).

Non-goals
- Fully bespoke per-customer autotuning beyond the three tiers.
- Major algorithmic scheduler changes (use existing batching/scheduling mechanisms).

Design references
- Confluence PRD: workload-aware batching defaults PRD
- Confluence design spec: workload-aware batching defaults design spec
- ADR-041: SLO tiered batching profiles

Implementation plan (v1)

A) Inputs / precedence
Effective parameters must be computed using the following precedence order:
1. Explicit per-route/per-model batching knobs (legacy fields like `max_batch_size`, `max_queue_delay_ms`, etc.)
2. Tier-derived defaults (this ticket)
3. Legacy runtime defaults (status quo)

`batching_tier` is optional. If not set, no behavior change (continue legacy defaults unless a control-plane default is applied by product/config later).

B) Workload signals (v1)
Signals are computed per “scheduler policy key” = (route_type, model_id/model_family, streaming_flag, gpu_sku). Where available, use recent-window stats; otherwise fall back to request-local classification.
- route_type: chat/completions vs embeddings/rerank (embeddings treated separately; generally allow larger batches, higher queue delay)
- streaming_flag: streaming true/false
- prompt_length_bucket: derived from request prompt token count (bucketed: 0–512, 513–2k, 2k–8k, 8k+)
- concurrency/arrival pressure: lightweight signal from in-flight queue depth + recent arrivals (no heavy estimator; use existing counters)
- model_family: from model metadata (e.g., “llama”, “mixtral”, “qwen”; exact mapping maintained by model registry)
- gpu_sku: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40S, etc.

C) Parameter mapping
Compute an intermediate “target aggressiveness” based on tier:
- fast: prioritize token latency and streaming cadence; minimize queue delay; smaller batches; decode priority
- standard: balanced; moderate queue delay and batch sizes
- cost_efficient: maximize throughput/$; allow more queueing and larger batches, but must respect overload protection + tail latency guardrails

Parameters produced by the tier mapping (names are representative; use actual runtime names):
- `max_batch_size` (cap)
- `max_queue_delay_ms` (cap)
- `prefill_decode_weight` or equivalent scheduling weights
- `kv_cache_pressure_limit` (or per-stage memory pressure clamp used by the scheduler)
- `admission_control` thresholds / backpressure behavior (integration point with overload protection; actual shedding policy is handled by ENG-18424/PR)

Guardrails / clamps (apply after mapping and after model/GPU overrides):
- If streaming=true, clamp `max_queue_delay_ms` to a lower ceiling per tier (fast < standard < cost_efficient) to protect cadence.
- If prompt_length_bucket >= 8k, reduce `max_batch_size` and tighten KV cache pressure thresholds (avoid OOM + pathological prefill contention).
- If concurrency is low (under-utilization), reduce queue delay to avoid “waiting for batches that never form”.
- Always keep params within hard-coded safety bounds (min/max) so a bad registry entry can’t set obviously dangerous values.

D) Model/GPU overrides
Runtime should accept an optional override blob from the model registry keyed by (model_family, gpu_sku, tier). If missing, use compiled-in defaults.
- Overrides must be versioned (model registry handles auditability); runtime should include version/hash in debug logs/spans.
- If override values violate safety bounds, emit a warning and clamp.

E) Observability (runtime-side)
Emit structured debug fields on the request trace span (or per-batch span) including:
- requested tier + final effective tier (if any normalization is applied)
- signal snapshot (streaming flag, prompt bucket, concurrency signal)
- final effective values for: max_batch_size, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill/decode weights, kv cache pressure limit
- “source” attribution per parameter (explicit override vs tier default vs registry override vs legacy)

Metrics are tracked in ENG-18422; this ticket should ensure the mapping code paths annotate spans and expose the values to metrics labels where appropriate (without exploding cardinality).

Acceptance criteria
Functional
- Given `batching_tier=fast|standard|cost_efficient`, runtime deterministically computes an effective parameter set using the mapping + guardrails.
- Explicit batching knob(s) in config override the tier-derived value(s) for the same parameter, without changing other tier-derived defaults.
- If `batching_tier` is absent, there is no behavior change vs legacy defaults.
- Streaming requests do not exceed the streaming queue-delay clamp for the selected tier.
- Long-context (8k+) requests reduce batch size appropriately and avoid known OOM-prone settings.
- Runtime logs/spans include “effective params” + parameter source attribution.

Quality / performance safety
- No regression in baseline latency for non-tiered traffic (tier unset).
- For tiered traffic, changes are behind a feature flag and can be enabled per model/region by rollout tooling.
- Works with overload protection: cost_efficient tier must not bypass admission control (integration validated with ENG-18424).

Test plan
Unit tests (runtime)
- Mapping table tests: for each tier + route_type + streaming flag + prompt bucket, verify expected parameter outputs (goldens).
- Precedence tests: explicit overrides win; partial overrides only override specific knobs.
- Guardrail tests: streaming clamp enforced; long-context clamp enforced; safety bounds clamp enforced.
- Registry override tests: override applied when present; clamped when out of bounds; version recorded.

Integration tests
- Config parsing + tier selection end-to-end in staging runtime: exercise chat/completions + embeddings.
- Verify trace annotations include the computed fields.

Performance validation hooks (owned by perf-canary, but required for this ticket)
- Add a small deterministic microbenchmark in CI that verifies tier mapping overhead is negligible (no per-request heavy computation).

Rollout
- Land behind feature flag `tiered_batching_defaults_v1` (exact name to match rollout primitives).
- Initial enablement targets: subset of hosted models in 1 region; then expand.

Deliverables
- Runtime code implementing tier selection + mapping + guardrails.
- Unit tests.
- Links to PRs and perf results.

Links
- Related PRs: redwood/pr_18435, redwood/pr_18527, redwood/pr_18539
- Follow-ups: effective-config explain endpoint (redwood/pr_18470), metrics (redwood/pr_18449), streaming cadence fix (redwood/pr_18463)
comments: 2025-02-11 (Sofia Ivanova): Marking P0. We need runtime-side mapping early so SRE can define tier SLO dashboards with real labels/fields. Please keep mapping deterministic + easy to diff in reviews. Tie to ADR-041.

2025-02-14 (Marcus Reed): Drafted mapping table for chat/completions vs embeddings. Question: do we treat tool-calls as chat (yes) but clamp queue delay more aggressively due to cancellation patterns? I’ll keep v1 same as streaming clamp; revisit after canary data.

2025-02-18 (Lena Fischer): +1 on tool-call handling. Also please ensure partial overrides work cleanly: e.g., customer sets max_batch_size explicitly but wants tier to still drive queue delay + weights.

2025-02-21 (Omar El-Sayed): Heads up: KV cache pressure thresholds are currently expressed as “target_free_mem_ratio” internally. If we map to a new higher-level knob, make sure we don’t invert semantics. I can help review.

2025-02-26 (Sean Gallagher): From SLO side: streaming cadence is the #1 concern. Please enforce a hard clamp for streaming in fast tier. We can’t rely on overload protection to save cadence if we queue too long.

2025-03-01 (Marcus Reed): Implemented mapping + clamps behind `tiered_batching_defaults_v1`. Added source attribution per parameter (explicit/tier/registry/legacy) to trace fields. Unit tests in place; sending to Sofia + Omar for review.

2025-03-04 (Sofia Ivanova): Review notes: (1) Ensure prompt bucket calc is based on prompt_tokens only (not total). (2) Clamp registry overrides BEFORE source attribution is recorded; we want to see ‘registry(clamped)’ in spans. (3) Please avoid adding high-cardinality labels to metrics; keep detailed values in traces only.

2025-03-07 (Marcus Reed): Addressed review notes. Prompt bucket is prompt-only. Added ‘registry_clamped=true’ field. No numeric params exported as metric labels; only tier + route_type + streaming. Ready to merge.

2025-03-11 (Rafael Mendes): For rollout: please confirm that when tier unset we truly preserve legacy. We’ll ramp standard tier by default later via control-plane; but right now we can’t afford surprise changes.
2025-03-12 (Marcus Reed): Confirmed in staging: tier unset path bypasses mapper entirely. Added explicit unit test asserting legacy defaults are identical (snapshot) when tier unset.

2025-03-18 (Sofia Ivanova): Marking Done. Merged via redwood/pr_18435 + follow-up refactor redwood/pr_18527; memory pressure edge-case addressed in redwood/pr_18539. Next: perf canary expansion (ENG-18423) and overload protection alignment (ENG-18424).
